Fireworks
During many holidays and events, fireworks are a common (0) _, adding a
colourful element to Malaysian culture. Whether it is Chinese New Year, Deepavali, or Eid Al-Fitr,
fireworks are enjoyed (9) ____________ individuals of all ages to enhance the cheerful atmosphere.
Fireworks are often (10) _ at pop-up stalls along the streets and in night markets with no
proper control and regulation.
Although fireworks bring about fun and excitement, they also give (11) ____________. to several
public concerns. One of the primary dangers is the potential for accidents and injuries. The incorrect
and careless (12) _ _ of fireworks, whether by youths or inexperienced adults, can lead to
severe burns, eye injuries, and even permanent disabilities. Furthermore, the loud noises produced
by fireworks can cause distress to those who (13) _ sensitive to loud noises, for instance,
babies, young children, the elderly and pets.
To address these concerns and ensure public safety, several measures can be
(14) ____________ -. Firstly, there should be (15) _ regulations on the sale and use of
fireworks, including minimum age requirements and compulsory permits for selling them. Public
awareness campaigns can also be conducted to (16) _ individuals about the dangers of
fireworks and promote alternative forms of celebration that do not pose risks to public safety and the
environment. Moreover, communities can organise controlled fireworks displays conducted by
trained licensed professionals, providing a safe and controlled environment for the general public to
enjoy the show (17) ____________ putting themselves or others in danger.
In conclusion, while fireworks have long been seen as an essential (18) ____________ - ~ of
Malaysian celebrations, their use comes with significant risks and drawbacks that cannot be ignored.
To ensure the well-being of individuals and the environment, it is imperative to consider the
arguments for their banning and implement strict measures to control their sale and use.

3.text:
Part 3
Questions 19 to 26
You are going to read an extract from an article. For questions 19 to 26, choose the correct
answer (A, B, C, or D) and mark the correct letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
A recent report from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) indicates that
the country has reached a warning level of extreme dry and hot weather conditions in the north of
Peninsula Malaysia. The report states that the condition with temperature exceeding 35 degrees
Celsius could be expected for three consecutive days starting August 13. The affected states are
Perlis, Kedah and Penang.
Department Director of the Malaysian Ministry of Health, Datuk Dr Harliza Abdul Rashid said
people should lessen outdoor activities during hot weather, wear lighter clothes and use umbrellas
and hats to avoid direct exposure to the sun. "Scorching weather can cause the individual to feel
lethargic and increase the risk for dehydration and heat stroke," she told Bernama, adding that
people should drink at least eight glasses of water daily to stay cool and hydrated. The ministry has
also issued a statement that people may feel increasingly heat stressed and this may affect their
health and reduce economic activity.
More people are seeking shelter from the heat by staying at home or going to air-conditioned
shopping malls. On the other hand, small businesses like hawkers and street vendors are left
deserted. With fewer customers venturing out in the heat, these small businesses are facing a dire
situation, teetering on the brink of closure.
This is almost the case for Fahim Anuar. Born into a family of hawkers, Fahim inherited the
trade from his parents, who owned a small fried noodles stall in Sungai Petani. From the young age
of 14, he learned the art of cooking from his mother and he has been cooking ever since. Fahim's
dream is to feed as many people as he can by selling his food at an affordable price. He understands
the poverty and hardships of making ends meet, growing up in a low-income household. Despite the
rising cost of living, Fahim has kept his prices consistent since 2004 when he first started, staying
true to his commitment to providing accessible meals to his community
Now, the extreme heatwave that sweeps across the nation has taken its toll on Fahim and
his fellow hawkers, turning their workplace into a furnace. The heat drives customers away and
leaves Fahim struggling to make ends meet. "There were days when the heat was so intense that |
thought about giving up," Fahim recalls, wiping the sweat from his brow. "But I knew I mustn't let
it defeat me." He stands tall behind his humble food cart in the street of Alor Setar, showing an
example of determination. As a hawker, Fahim's livelihood revolves around serving up steaming
plates of fried rice to hungry passersby.

Determined to rise above the heat, Fahim started experimenting with new recipes, adding
refreshing twists to traditional dishes to beat the heat. "From icy cold drinks to chilled desserts, I
found ways to keep my customers cool and satisfied," he explains. Once words spread, his stall
started drawing crowds to sample his new creations. Most of his customers are locals, with a few
tourists. While his signature fried rice still holds a special place in the hearts of loyal customers, his
customers now prefer his coconut lime shake and sour plum coconut jelly. They said the menu is
not only one of a kind, but also offers a better cooling effect on the body. Moreover, he also invested
in a canopy to provide shade for his customers and installed fans to keep them cool.
Today, Fahim Anuar stands as a shining example of what can be achieved by refusing to
surrender to life's challenges. "The heat may have tested me, but it also made me stronger," Fahim
says, gazing out at the busy street scene before him, "and for that, I am grateful."

4.text:
Part 4
Questions 27 to 32 are based on an article about teenage prisoners.
Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A to H the one
which fits each gap (27 to 32). There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use.
Mark your answers on the separate answer sheet.
When | arrived at Central Juvenile Hall, I was expecting guards and watch towers,
basically the setting of a cold and unfriendly place. I was told to wait in a small lobby room, which
separated the prison from the outside world. While waiting, I saw a few inmates getting on a bus.
They wore handcuffs and carried brown bags behind their backs. I looked at them, trying to guess
their crimes. 27
Inside Juvenile Hall, Mr. Javier Stauring, a warden at the prison came to accompany me
during the interview. I started getting nervous to think if my interview session with four of the juvenile
criminals would go well. We sat down on a bench in a small room. He told me that high-risk offenders
wore orange jumpsuits. He reminded me not to ask any sensitive questions regarding their past.
While we sat talking, a few teens walked by with a guard, their heads facing the ground
and their hands behind their backs. I was surprised by the innocence of their faces. I couldn't believe
my eyes when I saw a boy who looked like he was about ten, walking with handcuffed hands. I
realised | was grateful for having a normal life compared to those kids.
Soon, I met the four teens, and I found out just how bad their situations were.
29 Though the boys were the same age as me, they seemed older in their ways. They
had experienced a lot, and you could see it in the way they carried themselves. I was also shocked
when two pretty girls walked into the room. 30 L But, they still smiled and said hello to me.
Three of them said that leaving home at a young age was the only thing they could do
to save themselves from their broken homes. They admitted mixing with bad company and made
some bad choices. 31 This is especially true when it comes to where we live and who we
meet. It was simple for me to see that all four kids had no control over their lives. All they knew was
what made them feel better at the moment.
There are a lot of negative aspects about prison, but some positive things can come out
of being locked up. One of the boys mentioned that he has stayed out of trouble because of being
held in prison. 32 Moreover, being jailed allows these teens to stop and think. It also
creates a space for the juvenile criminals to put a brake and take a moment to think about their
future.
(Adapted from https://www.layouth.com/behind-bars-four-teens-in-prison-tell-their-stories/)

A Using their full names or taking pictures of their faces was also prohibited as they were underage.

B When I saw two of them first, they seemed calm and laid back.

C I began to think about some of the common offences that could have got them arrested.

D Prison, for many out-of-control teens, is stopping them from going further with a criminal and violent life.

E Both of them stared at me uncomfortably.

F While he looked like he had no regrets in life, sadness was written all over his face.

G What I learned from talking with them is that there are some things we have no control over.

H They were brought up this way, so that’s how they’re going to treat others.

Part 5
Questions 33 to 40
Here are six teenagers sharing their experiences at haunted places. Read the toxts below and
answer the questions that follow.
Teens at Haunted Places
A - ALAN, 16
When I watched the movie Shadewoods (2023) with my cousin, I was a bit sceptical to hear that
it was based on actual events at a theme park. However, this changed after my visit there earlier
this year. My knees turned to jelly when the cleaning lady shared her personal experience about
how the workers had to deal with shaken crew members who experienced ghostly incidents
during filming.
B - BYRON, 17
Curiosity drove me and my friend to stay in this creepy 24-storey apartment. According to
rumours, guests had been seeing a headless woman walking around the building. Last year, an
actor who starred in his latest film, Nightmare Hotel almost quit during the production of the
movie there after seeing the woman twice. Too bad we didn't come across any scary incidents
there.
C-CONNIE, 18
I'm one of the many people who had strange encounters on one of Malaysia's most haunted
highways. I remember one night, my family and I started to break into a cold sweat when we
saw a driverless yellow Volkswagen overtaking us on this highway. The Parak Highway's
hauntings are so widely known that a horror movie titled Parak: The Devil's Route was produced
in 2011.
D - DENVER, 15
Two years ago, my friends and | stayed in the infamous seafront villa known as The Echoing
Waves, where a man was said to have taken the lives of his whole family members. All six of us
cramped up in a room as it was recommended to stay together when visiting this place. Still, we
sensed as though someone was watching us. It felt so real!
E - ELLIE, 14
There was a place in my hometown that was used as a military office building during the
Japanese Occupation. People were said to have been tortured to their deaths there. I remember
having goosebumps when I drove past this scary-looking building. I heard that there had even
been reports of sudden attacks of hysteria taking over visitors at the site.
F - FIONA, 16
Last year, I visited Gloomhaven Mansion, a 50-year-old mansion, which was said to be the site
used by a well-known witch doctor. Some locals claimed to have heard unexplained growling
sounds coming from the surrounding areas of the building. They believe they're the sounds of
his evil spirits. My blood ran cold from hearing the stories, so | followed their advice not to stay
within the area past sundown.
